h2: NDT training in Virginia: shipyard apprenticeships, college courses and online study compared
html:
NDT training in Virginia: shipyard apprenticeships, college courses and online study compared

Most Virginia searches for NDT training come from Hampton Roads, where shipbuilding and ship repair employ a large inspection workforce, but the state also has power generation, manufacturing, pipelines and construction spread from Richmond to the Shenandoah Valley and Southwest Virginia. The right route depends on where you live and whether you can get a place in an employer program.

Who offers NDT training around Virginia?

  • The Apprentice School at Newport News Shipbuilding. Lists non-destructive tester among its apprentice trades, combining paid shipyard work with academic instruction. Places are competitive, and the training is built around the shipyard's own requirements.
  • Tidewater Community College. Offers a Nondestructive Inspection and Testing course within its industrial technology offerings, a useful introduction for welders and technicians in South Hampton Roads.
  • Ship repair, defense and inspection contractors. Companies supporting naval and commercial ship work, power plants and pipelines hire trainees and certify them under their own written practice once they have the required hours.
  • Self-paced online theory with an employer practical. Suits technicians in Richmond, Lynchburg, Roanoke and other areas far from the shipyard programs, and anyone already employed who needs a new method.

Which route fits you?

Your situationRoute that usually fitsWhat to check
Starting out in Hampton RoadsA shipyard apprenticeship or a college introduction followed by a trainee roleApplication windows and whether the role logs NDT method hours
Working technician outside Hampton RoadsSelf-paced method course plus the practical at workThat your employer's written practice accepts the course hours
Contractor on naval workTraining aligned to the contract's personnel requirementsWhich qualification standard the contract names
Employer certifying a crewOn-site training at your facilityWritten practice status and who administers the examinations

How the picture changes across Virginia

Hampton Roads, covering Newport News, Norfolk, Portsmouth and Chesapeake, holds most of the state's NDT employment through shipbuilding, ship repair and the contractors around them, and it is where the apprenticeship and college routes are. Richmond and the I-95 corridor have chemical, tobacco-equipment, power and construction work, with technicians usually trained by employers or contractors. Central and Southwest Virginia, from Lynchburg to Roanoke and the coalfields, include nuclear supply chain manufacturing, power generation and rail, where method training is mostly done on the job. Northern Virginia has a large data center construction market where structural steel and welding inspection are in demand, and where welding inspection credentials are often asked for alongside NDT methods.

Wherever you are, the deciding factor is usually the employer. A company that will record your supervised hours and certify you under its written practice matters more than which classroom you sat in.

Questions to ask any NDT training provider in Virginia

  1. How many hours of classroom instruction does each method course provide?
  2. Does the work you are targeting follow SNT-TC-1A, or does a naval or customer contract name another qualification standard?
  3. Who runs the practical and on what parts?
  4. Who certifies you afterwards? A training provider does not; your employer does under SNT-TC-1A.
  5. How do you reach a Level III with questions during the course?

Virginia is an NRC Agreement State, and the Virginia Department of Health licenses the radioactive materials used for industrial radiography. An RT theory course does not license anyone to use a source.

Where Atlantis fits for Virginia candidates and employers

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Virginia. Theory is self-paced online with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions in writing, and courses run year-round, so a candidate can start the day they enrol. Practicals are rehearsed in the Practical NDT simulator and done in person at the employer's own facility under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A; employers can have the training delivered on-site.

Read about Level 1 and Level 2 training, the visual testing and ultrasonic testing courses common in ship and weld work, and the six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course for welding inspectors. City pages for Norfolk and Newport News cover Hampton Roads employers, and the eligibility checker shows the hours each level needs.
